claims.exact_statement: In the single-cluster hard-step-force model (beta=infinity), before force turns on, the m process is a birth-death chain with lambda_m=(L-m)kon and mu_m=m(ka0+kb0), independent of extracted-antigen count n. Starting at m=1, the probability of hitting mc before zero is [1+sum_{j=1}^{mc-1} product_{r=1}^j mu_r/lambda_r]^-1 for L>=mc and is zero for L<mc.
assumptions: shared constant association rate kon for fresh binding and rebinding
absorbing zero before threshold; no tmin restart
claims.novelty_boundary: A scoped birth-death calculation for a model parameterization, not a new biological law; it does not imply finite-beta thresholding or final-score dose invariance.
costs: requires L, kon, ka0, kb0, and mc to evaluate
does not charge controller sensing or force-generation work
claims.falsifier: An exact pre-force CTMC with these transition rates gives a different threshold-hit probability.
claims.next_gate: Measure force onset versus running maximum under independently controlled antigen count and membrane mobility.

claims.exact_statement: For the source model at Eb=13.3 kBT, deltaEb=0.5 kBT, L=100, F0=800 pN, beta=5, and mc=tc=60, the internally simulated source-style finite differences yield alphaE=2.771 and alphaL=0.00878 per ligand for F(mmax), versus alphaE=3.516 and alphaL=0.08784 per ligand for F(t); alphaL for deltaL=24 is .211 versus 2.108.
assumptions: published one-cluster Gillespie model and parameters
means use observed score by tmax
no censoring occurred in these local probe conditions
claims.novelty_boundary: Reproduces the source's local sensitivity concept; does not establish a new result about B-cell discrimination.
costs: no physical force-displacement work or ATP measured
claims.falsifier: Independent exact source-code replay at these parameters falls outside the Monte Carlo uncertainty for the reported means and ratios.
claims.next_gate: Report the full finite-dose distribution and matched-dose ranking, not only local alphaL.

claims.exact_statement: Within the reconstructed published model, a running-maximum force policy improves affinity ranking under independently drawn, broad dose distributions in these finite scans, but the advantage is prior-dependent and is absent or reversed for affinity pairs matched at the same dose; it is therefore not a universal finite-dose guarantee.
assumptions: source one-cluster model and stopping rules
adaptive source schedule uses F0=800 pN, beta=5
two independently drawn dose scores or same-dose pairs as specified
adaptive threshold chosen from a finite seven-value grid
for independently drawn doses, time-only controller knows the same prior and is screened on 5x7 (F0,tc), with top two schedules validated on a fresh stream
matched-dose diagnostic uses time settings selected in the initial 3x3 scan and does not optimize F(t) specifically for matched-dose ranking
tmax=1800s censor is retained and bounded separately
claims.status: finite computation; scoped refutation of universal-robustness route
claims.novelty_boundary: The qualitative adaptive mechanical proofreading principle is already published in PRX Life (2026); this audit is neither a new mechanism nor a biological validation. Alternative uniform priors are stress tests, not measured in vivo distributions.
costs: 4000-pair fresh validation of top two time schedules and 4000-pair adaptive reference per prior; separate 5000-pair independent/matched reruns
finite parameter grid, not global optimization; adaptive force ceiling held at source 800 pN
AUC MC intervals are approximate normal intervals
censored score envelopes can be wide
claims.falsifier: A faithful, higher-precision model replay with a globally optimized prior-aware time-only policy reverses the stated numerical ordering for all named settings; biological transfer additionally requires measured-cell data.
claims.next_gate: Perform the factorial held-out-dose/mobility experiment in restart_gates/EXPERIMENT.md and optimize the time-only baseline on the same data and true-work constraint.

claims.exact_statement: Antigen-presenting membrane mobility is an experimentally measured confound for a dose-only mechanical-proofreading model: it changes force timing/location/magnitude, antigen extraction speed, and affinity discrimination in B-cell immune synapses.
assumptions: scope limited to the tested primary B cells, DNA-nanostructure NIP antigen and DOPC/DPPC supported bilayers in McArthur et al. 2025
claims.status: established external within the named experiment
claims.novelty_boundary: Source-reported experiment, not new work from this audit and not evidence for mmax force control.
costs: Requires mobility/tension imaging and controlled bilayers; exact quantitative assay cost not estimated.
claims.falsifier: A replication under the same substrate/antigen/B-cell conditions finds no reproducible mobility-dependent extraction or force-dynamics effect.
claims.next_gate: Treat measured mobility and accessible antigen pool as blocked factors in the proposed controller comparison.

overall_verdict: No defensible new immunology principle was established. The attractive mechanism is now published prior art; the best internal result is a scoped audit that identifies dose-prior and matched-dose failure modes plus an experiment that could distinguish mechanism from proxy. Do not present this as a clinical or biological discovery.
